Johncock, Mears the Stars So Far in 1982
Two drivers, Gordon Johncock and Rick
Mears, have dominated Indy Car racing thus far
in 1982.
Mears led off the season by setting track
records in qualifying and winning each of the
year's first two contests, the CART-sanctioned
Kraco 150 at Phoenix (Ariz.) International
Raceway on Mar. 28 and the Stroh's 200 at Atlan-
ta International Raceway (Hampton, Ga.) on
May 1.
Johncock, who placed fifth in the Phoenix
opener and second at Atlanta, snapped Mears'
winning streak in the USAC-sanctioned In-
dianapolis 500 on May 30, winning the event at
the Indianapolis Motor Speedway (Speedway,
Ind.) by .16 of a second over Mears. The finish
was the closest in the 66-year history of the
event.

Mosley Became the Seventh
V
Mike Mosley's triumph in the 1981 Gould Rex Mays Classic made
him the seventh repeat winner in the 32-year history of the event.
Mosley's previous Rex Mays victory came in 1976, when he
recorded the last wire-to-wire victory in Wisconsin State Fair Park
Speedway Indy Car competition.
Rodger Ward, the all-time winningest Milwaukee Mile Indy Car
pilot, and A.J. Foyt top the career Rex Mays Classic victory list with
four each.
Bobby Unser has three wins in the annual June classic, while
Mosley, Johnny Rutherford, Tony Bettenhausen and Johnny Thom-
